Q: Bar chart legends in R A:

A safe option would be to make a factor out of housing_density first, which avoids typos in manual approaches during plotting.

sub_21_24_df$housing_density <- 
  factor(sub_21_24_df$housing_density, 
         labels=c('rural', 'rural/suburb', 'suburb',  'city')
  )

which gives:

> sub_21_24_df
  housing_density  HOW_MANY
1           rural 276360784
2    rural/suburb   9233474
3          suburb  11659386
4            city   1905698

Be careful when assigning the factor labels, since they are assigned according to the alphabetical order of the values rather than the order in which they appear in the column, see:

> (x <- c(4, 3, 1, 2))
[1] 4 3 1 2
> factor(x, labels=c('rural', 'rural/suburb', 'suburb',  'city'))
[1] city         suburb       rural        rural/suburb
Levels: rural rural/suburb suburb city

Then consider how much complexity the visualization actually needs. Do I really need a legend, or might I display the labels just below the bars? Do I really need different colors, or are bars themselves already sufficiently visually distinct? Here a minimalist solution using barplot:

png('myplot.png')
barplot(
  sub_21_24_df$HOW_MANY/1e6, 
  col='black', 
  las=1,  ## makes y-axis labels horizontal
  ylab='Density (in millions)',
  names.arg=sub_21_24_df$housing_density
)
dev.off()

This should work similarly in ggplot2 if needed, I'll leave that up to you.

Data:

sub_21_24_df <- read.table(text='  housing_density  HOW_MANY
1               1 276360784
2               2   9233474
3               3  11659386
4               4   1905698')

Q: Why can I scrape some Fangraphs player tables with R but not others? A:

NULL is returned, if the xpath can't be found within url_read_html. Your xpath is correct, but read_html does not always get exactly the same webpage as you see within the browser. Some tables might be loaded in using a) calls to an API, b) running Javascript to parse that response and build a table dynamically. It could also be, that the webpage starts out with a Please accept these cookies-Section or Cloudflare-Challenge, in which case your tables do not exist.

Sadly, your code gives me an error

library(purrr)
library(rvest)
 
url_basallo <- "https://www.fangraphs.com/players/samuel-basallo/28824/stats/batting"
 
xpath_look <- '//*[@id="dashboard"]/div[3]/div/div/div/div[1]/table'
 
url_read_html <- 
   url_basallo |> 
   read_html() 

Error in open.connection(x, "rb") : Can't open connection

So let's try read_html_live to see what's going on

library(purrr)
library(rvest)

url_basallo <- "https://www.fangraphs.com/players/samuel-basallo/28824/stats/batting"

xpath_look <- '//*[@id="dashboard"]/div[3]/div/div/div/div[1]/table'

url_read_html <- 
  url_basallo |> 
  read_html_live() 

url_read_html |> 
  html_nodes(xpath = xpath_look)  |>
  html_table() |>
  pluck(1)

NULL

This returns NULL, so that DOM-element from the xpath does not exist. Let's look at what the Live_HTML session sees using

url_read_html$view()

That's a Cloudflare-Challenge. read_html_live actually opens a chromote session under the hood:

. So it opens an invisible browser in the background (headless) to navigate to the page, but it's stopped by Cloudflare. That's the reason why your tables do not show.

Alternative Solution using the API

Using this approach you can navigate to the page, solve the cloudflare manually and then get the cloudflare clearance-token cf_clearance from the cookies in the Request-Headers.

And then loop over all request-links using this token. This will give you the direct server-response data. Notes:

  • The clearance-token hold 30 min - mutliple hours at best
  • I did not get much into the inner works of the url-structure, but I found this

Code

library(httr2)

urls <- c(
  url_batting        = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/stats/batting.json?playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_splits         = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/splits.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_splits_tools   = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/splits-tool.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_pitch_type     = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/pitch-type-splits.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_game_log       = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/game-log.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_play_log       = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/play-log.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_graphs         = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/graphs.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_pitch_velocity = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/pitch-velocity-graphs.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_gamecharts     = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/game-charts.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824" ,
  url_spraycharts    = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/spray-charts.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_heatmpas       = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/heat-maps.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_fantasy_tools  = "https://www.fangraphs.com/_next/data/AqrsHP61GXGxiYukyX8Zv/players/samuel-basallo/28824/fantasy-tools.json?position=NP&playerNameRoute=samuel-basallo&playerId=28824",
  url_dates          = "https://www.fangraphs.com/api/players/game-log/dates?playerid=28824&position=NP"
)


fetch_fangraphs_data <- \(url, cf_clearance){
  
  if (missing(url)) stop("Please provide a value for url.") 
  if (missing(cf_clearance)) stop("Please provide a value for cf_clearance.")
  
  request(url) |>
    req_headers(
      "accept" = "*/*",
      "accept-language" = "en,de-DE;q=0.9,de;q=0.8",
      "cache-control" = "no-cache",
      "pragma" = "no-cache",
      "referer" = "https://www.fangraphs.com/players/samuel-basallo/28824/stats/batting",
      "sec-fetch-dest" = "empty",
      "sec-fetch-mode" = "cors",
      "sec-fetch-site" = "same-origin",
      "user-agent" = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/145.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",
      "dnt" = "1",
      "cookie" = sprintf("cf_clearance=%s", cf_clearance)
    ) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json()
}

data <- lapply(urls, \(x) {
  fetch_fangraphs_data(x, cf_clearance = "7tdXNENxT6I7rGJNU2MzBpZMO22kXRywTDcC.rNK2Jw-1772351364-1.2.1.1-D1yU7RXlY3X4VJ66Fo3dV5iAWYMNe7EULlBRA0XLoMPGjGVcIuwjfBuAZTUHeCWZXG5lf4x_Aa6rcBT781oxBpKSsPjksw_VzwsLNKk40IMf0T9qGbc7A0cYwBYKhFCrx.ZQvZw5O3rGBd_d5VE6qhZtUngQ6iml4qDvysuA5dBYvMbkQIa24tj8JRyH5ZCFJ2s5N45JjhHwt3CU3hhC93ex6BjR0tbS3ArrkKhxoms")
})

Q: Apache Camel Spring Boot Application native executable exception A:

I have read the Apache Camel 4.18 What's New blog.

In the Roadmap section it is reported that the goal of the next 4.19 release is to migrate to Spring Boot v4.

Therefore in my pom.xml I have downgraded to 3.5.11 the reference to the spring boot version and everything worked fine.

Q: Cannot upload binaries via GitHub release workflow A:

Disclosure: I don't use actions/create-release, softprops/actions-gh-release is the alternative I use.

You are setting the permissions on the GitHub token incorrectly. That needs to be done either on the workflow or job:

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

env:
  BUILD_TYPE: Release

jobs:
  build-and-release:
    runs-on: windows-latest

    # set your permission here
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Configure CMake
      run: cmake -B ${{github.workspace}}/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=${{env.BUILD_TYPE}}

    - name: Build
      run: cmake --build ${{github.workspace}}/build --config ${{env.BUILD_TYPE}}

    - name: Create GitHub Release
      id: create_release
      uses: actions/create-release@v1
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      with:
        tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        release_name: Release ${{ github.ref_name }}
        body: |
          Release created by GitHub Actions for tag ${{ github.ref_name }}.
        draft: false
        prerelease: false

    - name: Upload binaries to release
      uses: svenstaro/upload-release-action@v2
      with:
        repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        file: ${{github.workspace}}\.bin\${{env.BUILD_TYPE}}\ccecho.exe
        asset_name: ccecho-${{github.ref}}.exe
        tag: ${{ github.ref }}
        overwrite: true
        body: "Releasing echo server ${{github.ref}}"

Trying to set it inside the env only created two environment variables, permissions which was empty and contents=write, which doesn't do anything to the permissions.

Q: Enter key in textarea A:

We should most definitely not be using the .keyCode property. It is deprecated:

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/KeyboardEvent/keyCode

Instead of

event.keyCode === 13

Do it like

event.key === 'Enter'


const textarea = document.querySelector('textarea');
textarea.addEventListener('keypress', function (e) {
    if (e.key === 'Enter') { // also you can check && e.shiftKey
        e.preventDefault();
        alert('Enter pressed!');
    }
});
<textarea></textarea>

Q: How to request data from another security to show correctly with request.security() - Pine Script v5 - TradingView A:

syminfo.* variables are linked to the current chart and it's not possible to pass it in a security function. You need to do a work around. See the code below as an example.

// This source code is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public License 2.0 at https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/
// © Phwi
//@version=5
indicator("Get Prefix with out using syminfo.prefix", overlay = false)

comp_override = input(defval=false, title='Override Auto Detection of Index')
sym = input.symbol('OMXCOP:OMXC25', title='Index override')


f_BSMA(symbol) =>


    pos_start = str.pos(symbol, "")  // Get start position of ":" character
    pos_stop = str.pos(symbol, ":")  // Get position of ":" character. Stop position

    tkr= str.substring(symbol, pos_start, pos_stop) // Get Exchange
    
    ex = str.replace_all(str.replace_all(tkr, '_DLY', ''), '_DL', '')  // "_DLY" suffix in syminfo.prefix workaround

    //Get Indeks to compare to
    comparativeTickerId = comp_override and sym != '' ? sym : syminfo.type == 'index' ? 'NYSE:OOI' : syminfo.type == 'cfd' ? 'NYSE:OOI' : syminfo.type == 'forex' ? 'INDEX:DXY' : ex == 'LSE' ? 'UKXGBP' : ex == 'ASX' ? 'ASX:AST' : ex == 'OSL' ? 'OSL:OBX' : ex == 'OMXSTO' ? 'OMXSTO:OMXS30' : ex == 'OMXCOP' ? 'OMXCOP:OMXC25' : ex == 'OMXHEX' ? 'OMXHEX:OMXH25' : ex == 'OMXICE' ? 'OMXICE:OMXI10' : ex == 'XETR' ? 'XETR:DAX' : ex == 'FWB' ? 'XETR:DAX' : ex == 'SWB' ? 'XETR:DAX' : ex == 'EURONEXT' ? 'EURONEXT:PX1' : ex == 'EURONEXT' ? 'EURONEXT:AEX' : ex == 'EURONEXT' ? 'EURONEXT:BEL20' : ex == 'EURONEXT' ? 'EURONEXT:PSI20' : ex == 'DJCFD' ? 'AMEX:SPY' : ex == 'NYSE' ? 'AMEX:SPY' : ex == 'BATS' ? 'AMEX:SPY' : ex == 'NASDAQ' ? 'AMEX:SPY' : ex == 'OTC' ? 'AMEX:SPY' : sym  // last entry is the fallback, no match will default to the override ticker as comparison. by default OMXC25
  
   

    if barstate.islastconfirmedhistory
        label.new(bar_index, high, text =  comparativeTickerId)

   
f_BSMA(syminfo.tickerid)

Q: How to install swagger_client in a django project A:

This link clearly outlines things to be done. This is for anyone who is facing this issue

Download and install the API client library To execute the sample you need to generate the Python library for the REST API which is generated through Swagger.

Follow these steps for the installation:

Go to https://editor.swagger.io. Click File, then click Import URL. Enter the Swagger URL for the Speech Services API: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/main/specification/cognitiveservices/data-plane/Speech/SpeechToText/stable/v3.1/speechtotext.json. Click Generate Client and select Python. Save the client library. Extract the downloaded python-client-generated.zip somewhere in your file system. Install the extracted python-client module in your Python environment using pip: pip install path/to/package/python-client. The installed package has the name swagger_client. You can check that the installation worked using the command python -c "import swagger_client".

https://github.com/Azure-Samples/cognitive-services-speech-sdk/blob/master/samples/batch/python/README.md
